You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 477f3488a94e35380c82a7498d46f10fa5f3edd2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2020 06:53:00 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/6xx: Fix power_save_ppc32_restore() with
 CONFIG_VMAP_STACK

power_save_ppc32_restore() is called during exception entry, before
re-enabling the MMU. It substracts KERNELBASE from the address
of nap_save_msscr0 to access it.

With CONFIG_VMAP_STACK enabled, data MMU translation has already been
re-enabled, so power_save_ppc32_restore() has to access
nap_save_msscr0 by its virtual address.

Reported-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Fixes: cd08f109e262 ("powerpc/32s: Enable CONFIG_VMAP_STACK")
Tested-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/7bce32ccbab3ba3e3e0f27da6961bf6313df97ed.1581663140.git.christophe.leroy@c-s.fr

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S b/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S
index 0ffdd18b9f26..433d97bea1f3 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S
+++ b/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S
@@ -166,7 +166,11 @@ BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
 	mfspr	r9,SPRN_HID0
 	andis.	r9,r9,HID0_NAP@h
 	beq	1f
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_msscr0@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_msscr0@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_MSSCR0, r9
 	sync
@@ -174,7 +178,11 @@ BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
 1:
 END_FTR_SECTION_IFSET(CPU_FTR_NAP_DISABLE_L2_PR)
 BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_hid1@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_hid1-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_hid1@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_HID1, r9
 END_FTR_SECTION_IFSET(CPU_FTR_DUAL_PLL_750FX)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S`**
   - The patch modifies the assembly code in the `power_save_ppc32_restore()` function.
   - It introduces conditional compilation using `#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` to handle the access to `nap_save_msscr0` and `nap_save_hid1`.
   - When `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` is enabled, the code now accesses `nap_save_msscr0` and `nap_save_hid1` using their virtual addresses directly, instead of subtracting `KERNELBASE` from their addresses.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes are related to the handling of memory addresses in the context of the MMU (Memory Management Unit) state during exception entry.
- The introduction of the `#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` condition allows the code to adapt to different configurations of the kernel, specifically when the stack is virtualized.
- This modification ensures that the function correctly accesses the necessary data regardless of whether the MMU is enabled or not, thus fixing the bug reported by Larry Finger.

Here is the commit message:
powerpc/6xx: Fix power_save_ppc32_restore() with
 CONFIG_VMAP_STACK

power_save_ppc32_restore() is called during exception entry, before
re-enabling the MMU. It substracts KERNELBASE from the address
of nap_save_msscr0 to access it.

With CONFIG_VMAP_STACK enabled, data MMU translation has already been
re-enabled, so power_save_ppc32_restore() has to access
nap_save_msscr0 by its virtual address.

Reported-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Fixes: cd08f109e262 ("powerpc/32s: Enable CONFIG_VMAP_STACK")
Tested-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/7bce32ccbab3ba3e3e0f27da6961bf6313df97ed.1581663140.git.christophe.leroy@c-s.fr

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `power_save_ppc32_restore()` function attempts to access the `nap_save_msscr0` variable using a physical address calculation (subtracting `KERNELBASE`) when the MMU is not yet re-enabled. With `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` enabled, the data MMU translation is already active, requiring the function to access the variable using its virtual address instead. This mismatch leads to incorrect memory access during exception entry.

Here is the patch:
 	andis.	r9,r9,HID0_NAP@h
 	beq	1f
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_msscr0@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_msscr0@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_MSSCR0, r9
 END_FTR_SECTION_IFSET(CPU_FTR_NAP_DISABLE_L2_PR)
 BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_hid1@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_hid1-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_hid1@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_HID1, r9

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```assembly
addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
lwz	r9,nap_save_msscr0@l(r9)
```
Reason:
The `power_save_ppc32_restore()` function incorrectly calculates the address of `nap_save_msscr0` by subtracting `KERNELBASE`, which is appropriate only when the MMU is disabled. With `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` enabled, the data MMU translation is already active, making this physical address calculation invalid and leading to incorrect memory access.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```assembly
#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_msscr0@ha
#else
	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
#endif
```
Reason:
The patch introduces a conditional compilation directive that checks if `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` is enabled. If it is, the code accesses `nap_save_msscr0` using its virtual address directly, avoiding the incorrect physical address calculation. This ensures that the function correctly accesses the variable in the context of an already enabled MMU.
